title: Deadline and Ghost
premise: Mirabel Whitlock, a hostage negotiator haunted by the botched bank siege that killed an innocent bystander, receives a package from a stranger named Callum Reyes who claims she once saved his life — a favor she has no memory of. He demands repayment: use her access to expose a chemical plant 'accident' being staged by her own agency's director to bury evidence of corruption, with hundreds of workers as collateral. As Mirabel investigates and finds his claims true, she falls for Callum while torn between duty and justice; in the end she broadcasts the director's confession during the staged attack, talks him down from detonating it herself, and chooses to walk away from the badge — with Callum, into a life that finally feels like hers.
about_author: Edmund Vasquez is the pen name of a former crisis-line counselor who spent a decade listening to people at their worst moments before turning those voices into fiction. He writes thrillers about ordinary professionals pushed past the edge of procedure, and lives quietly somewhere on the Atlantic coast.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. After another successful negotiation, she returns home to find a package containing photos of the bank siege that broke her career — and proof the 'bystander' death was staged. A stranger, Callum Reyes, calls claiming she saved his life that day and now he's calling in the debt. The emotional beat is dread mixed with a dangerous flicker of hope that her guilt might be misplaced.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Mirabel and Callum. Mirabel verifies the documents against her own sealed case file while Callum reveals he was the scapegoated plant safety inspector. They uncover Director Hale's plan to trigger a gas leak at Corven Chemical to destroy records, scheduled for Friday. The beat is rising paranoia and reluctant trust as two liars decide to believe each other.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes of Static
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, climax. Inside the plant under cover of a routine inspection, Mirabel confronts Hale mid-sabotage, using every negotiation trick she owns while Callum races to evacuate the night shift. She goads Hale into confessing on an open line, then talks him back from the detonator as sirens rise. The beat is white-knuckle tension resolving into exhausted triumph.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Living
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, resolution. Weeks later, testifying under immunity, Mirabel watches Hale fall and faces the board that once discarded her — and declines reinstatement. She meets Callum at the pier where he first watched the bank burn, returning his 'favor' with interest: a fresh start neither earned but both accept. The beat is quiet belonging, love chosen over duty.
